subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which list places the metals in order from most reactive to least reactive?
questions.explain: Going down the reactivity series the order is potassium, then magnesium, then zinc, then copper.

questions.q: Which of these metals is the least reactive?
questions.explain: Gold is at the bottom of the reactivity series, making it the least reactive listed.

questions.q: What happens to a catalyst during a reaction?
options: It becomes part of the product
It is chemically unchanged at the end
questions.explain: A catalyst is not used up and remains chemically unchanged after the reaction.

questions.q: Which graph result shows that a reaction has finished?
options: The line falls back to zero
questions.explain: When no more product forms the line levels off (becomes horizontal), showing the reaction is complete.

questions.q: Which metal could be used to extract iron from iron oxide by displacement?
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than iron, so it can displace iron from iron oxide.

questions.q: For an exothermic forward reaction at equilibrium, increasing the temperature will:
options: Shift the equilibrium towards the reactants
Shift the equilibrium towards the products
questions.explain: Le Chatelier: raising temperature favours the endothermic direction, here the reverse (reactant) side.

questions.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It increases the concentration of reactants
It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
questions.explain: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

questions.q: At a higher temperature, a greater proportion of colliding particles:
options: Have at least the activation energy
Have less than the activation energy
questions.explain: Heating gives more particles energy equal to or above the activation energy, so more collisions succeed.

questions.q: A reactive metal can be extracted from its molten compound by electrolysis because:
options: Electricity decomposes the compound, depositing the metal
The metal melts and floats off
Carbon is more reactive than the metal
questions.explain: Electrolysis uses electricity to break down the compound, releasing the metal at the cathode.

questions.q: In the reactivity series, which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium is near the top of the reactivity series, far above iron, zinc and copper.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, oxidation is best described as:
questions.explain: Using OILRIG, Oxidation Is Loss of electrons.

questions.q: Calcium reacts with cold water to produce calcium hydroxide and which gas?
questions.explain: A metal reacting with water gives a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: In a displacement reaction, the more reactive metal:
questions.explain: The more reactive metal loses electrons to form ions, so it is oxidised.

questions.q: Some unreactive metals such as gold are found in the Earth as:
questions.explain: Very unreactive metals like gold are so unreactive they are found as the uncombined native metal.

questions.q: Why are alloys such as steel usually harder than the pure metal?
options: The atoms are all identical and slide easily
Different sized atoms distort the layers so they cannot slide easily
questions.explain: Different sized atoms in an alloy distort the regular layers, making it harder for them to slide.

questions.q: In the reaction CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, what happens to the copper oxide?
questions.explain: The copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced.

questions.q: The symbol ⇌ in an equation shows that the reaction is:
questions.explain: The ⇌ symbol indicates a reversible reaction.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, the magnesium has been:
questions.explain: Magnesium gains oxygen and loses electrons, so it is oxidised.

questions.q: Why does a reaction generally slow down over time even without changing conditions?
options: The reactant concentration decreases as it is used up
questions.explain: As reactants are consumed, their concentration falls, so collisions are less frequent and the rate decreases.

questions.q: If the concentration of a reactant is increased in a system at equilibrium, the equilibrium shifts to:
questions.explain: Adding more reactant shifts the equilibrium towards the products to oppose the change.

questions.q: Which mixture would NOT react, because no displacement is possible?
questions.explain: Copper is less reactive than zinc, so it cannot displace zinc from its solution.

questions.q: Decreasing the concentration of a product in a system at equilibrium causes the equilibrium to shift towards the:
questions.explain: Removing product makes the equilibrium shift towards the products to replace what was lost.
